carnage.name: TurbodTalon
carnage.commentary: The damage showed up on 11: a 7, which is a full four over and the kind of par-3 math that makes the card look like it got hit by a truck.

carnage.name: Rhino
carnage.commentary: 10 was the crater: a 6 on a par 3, three over, and the kind of miss that turns a card into a crime scene.

carnage.name: JStrawzzz
carnage.commentary: 17 was the ugly one: 5 gross, 6 net, and a three-over net disaster when a par-3 hole was begging for survival.

carnage.name: DLudGolf
carnage.commentary: 10 was the only real bruise on the card, a 4 gross and 5 net on a par 3 that still counts as a two-over net leak.

carnage.name: BogeyBro
carnage.commentary: 6 was the hiccup: a 4 on a par 3, one over, just enough to remind the card it’s still a par-3 league.

carnage.name: CrushGolf
carnage.commentary: 2 was the leak: a 4 on a par 3, one over, and the sort of early-round tax that keeps the number from looking cleaner.

players.name: BogeyBro
players.tagline: Built a decent card and still found a way to leave a little grease on it.
players.body: BogeyBro finished 25th net at +4, with a gross score of -4 that says the raw swing was fine and the scoring math just didn’t love the full package. The profile actually looks pretty sturdy underneath: +1.76 approach, +1.77 short game, +1.96 putting, and +5.50 total is a legit positive day. He hit 11 greens, rolled it well with 24 putts, and made 86 feet of putts, but the birdie count only got to five while the card still carried one bogey. The worst hole was 6, where he made 4 on a par 3, and that was enough to keep this from being a clean little pop-up round. With zero prior starts in the file, this is just the current round talking, and it’s saying he can definitely pile up value without exactly flushing the card into submission.

players.name: JStrawzzz
players.tagline: Fought the ball, fought the short game, then let the putter pretend it was innocent.
players.body: JStrawzzz came home 26th net at +5, while the gross finish at +2 shows the card had some usable juice even if the net side never really got settled. The split was classic chaos: -0.43 approach, -3.28 short game, but a loud +3.21 putting to drag the total back to only -0.50. He had 10 GIR, 27 putts, one three-putt, and 111 feet of putts made, so the flat stick did its job while the tee-to-green side ate the bill. The worst hole was 17, a 5 gross and 6 net on a par 3, which was the cleanest proof that the round could still kick him in the teeth after the putter gave him some cover. With no prior starts here, this is round-only evidence; the round screams volatility, not identity.

players.name: CrushGolf
players.tagline: Tee-to-green did the heavy lifting while the putter threw a tiny tantrum.
players.body: CrushGolf finished 27th net at +5, but the gross line of -1 is the important tell: the raw golf was actually playable, just not clean enough to cash in on the net board. He posted +2.09 approach and +0.77 short game with a respectable +2.86 tee-to-green, and the only drag was a -0.36 putting number that kept the total at +2.50 from looking better than the finish. The card had 10 GIR, 26 putts, no three-putts, and only four birdies, which fits a round that did some things right and still didn’t separate. The worst hole was 2, where he made 4 on a par 3, and that early leak is basically the story: not a meltdown, just enough dumb tax to keep the round stuck in the mud. With zero prior starts, there’s no trend to sell here—just one round that says the ball-striking was ahead of the result.

players.name: TurbodTalon
players.tagline: Found birdies, then paired them with a couple of full-blown faceplants.
players.body: TurbodTalon was 28th net at +5, and the gross finish at +4 shows a round that had enough scoring to hang around but also enough wreckage to keep the number muddy. The underlying stuff is wildly split: -2.87 approach and -3.04 tee to green, but +2.54 putting and seven birdies kept the card from going totally off the rails. Nine GIR, 25 putts, one three-putt, and two doubles tell the real story: this was not a tidy round, it was a patchwork quilt. The worst hole was 11, where he made 7 on a par 3, a four-over gross kick in the teeth that pretty much defined the ugly side of the day. With no prior starts on file, this is just the current mess on the table, and the current mess is loud.

players.name: Rhino
players.tagline: The putter showed up, but the rest of the bag got mugged in the alley.
players.body: Rhino finished 29th net at +5, and the gross result of +5 is the part that really stings because the scoring engine never got enough help from the rest of the bag. He was actually +2.42 putting and got away with 23 putts, but the tee-to-green side was a wreck at -5.92, including -4.43 short game and -1.50 approach. Seven GIR, 61 feet of putts made, and two doubles paint the picture: the flat stick kept it from being worse, but the misses around the greens and the extra damage on the card did the rest. The worst hole was 10, a 6 on a par 3, which was the cleanest example of the round getting kicked over. With zero prior starts, there’s no history to lean on; just one round where the putter tried to save the furniture and the rest of the house was already on fire.

players.name: DLudGolf
players.tagline: Ball-struck it like a madman and still made the scorecard do yoga.
players.body: DLudGolf finished 30th net at +5, but the gross finish at 13th and -5 to par tells you the raw golf was miles better than the net result. He smashed the ball-striking side with +3.94 approach, +2.85 short game, and a ridiculous +6.79 tee to green, plus 15 GIR and seven birdies. The issue was the rest of the card: 28 putts, a -0.29 putting number, and the net board refusing to reward the fireworks. Even the worst hole was only a 4 gross and 5 net on 10, which is basically a speed bump compared to the rest of the round. With zero prior starts, this is pure round-level evidence, and it says the game was there; the conversion was not. That’s golf for you: sometimes you hit it like a genius and still finish behind a guy who spent the day making pars with a shovel.
